title: A 10-year sentence for Bell
article: At the hearing, Crown prosecutor Bob Morrison compared Bell and her ex-lover Robert Sand to the infamous pair of American robbers. "This was Bonnie and Clyde on a crime spree."
Sand was previously convicted of first-degree murder with no chance of parole for 25 years for the Dec. 21, 2001, shooting of Strongquill, a 52-year-old father of six.
During Bell's sentencing, Morrison presented evidence of jailhouse love letters written by Bell to Sand during the three- month murder trial.
"I don't think you are cold nor heartless," Bell told Sand. "I think you are a strong man with passions like a wildfire."

Bell, 21, and Sand, 24, met in Edmonton in early December 2001, only a few weeks before the shooting. Sand helped Bell beat her drug addiction, then the two set off on a cross-country crime spree with Sand's brother Danny, 20.
They stole and torched vehicles, robbed a bank and broke into a home, accumulating an arsenal of 11 rifles and more than 1,000 rounds of ammunition.

Strongquill and his partner Brian Auger pulled over their vehicle for a routine traffic violation, after which Robert Sand opened fire on the police. When the police fled, Danny Sand chased the cruiser into the town of Russell, Man., then rammed the cruiser. Robert then gunned down Strongquill. Bell was in the backseat at the time.

Justice John Menzies said Robert and Danny Sand have already paid for shooting Strongquill -- Robert is in prison for life, and Danny was shot dead by RCMP snipers during the trio's arrest in Wolseley.
Bell was given double credit for the 18 months she's already served, meaning three years is knocked off her sentence. She will serve seven more years.
The judge called the slaying an abhorrent crime, but he said Bell wasn't the shooter and didn't intend for anyone to die. He called her a misguided individual, but not a hardened criminal.
Bell no longer has feelings for Sand, said her lawyer Brian Midwinter, mainly as a result of Sand's assault on his own lawyer in the courtroom at the end of the trial.
